findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the predicted side: the slope of the drift-adjusted 20-day return on the forecast's size has t -2.92 over 112 cases. The supporting mean misses the bar at t -1.96 on 36 days. In folds B and C alone (38 cases on 15 days) the mean is -8.2 % with t -1.38 and the slope t is -1.90, so the effect points the predicted way but is too thin to show clearly.
findings.F2: In folds B and C the effect sits in one window. The 13 cases of w18 average -21.6 % over 20 days against drift. The other 25 cases average -1.3 % (t -0.22), and w14 and w16 (11 cases) go the wrong way at +13.0 % and +12.4 %.
findings.F3: The grading is not steady across the rally's size. By tercile of the forecast, the 20-day excess return is -5.8 % (low), -5.6 % (mid) and -13.1 % (high), 12 to 13 cases each. At 30 days the low tercile (-11.1 %) falls more than the high one (-7.4 %).
findings.F4: No other horizon gives a clear and graded answer:
findings.F5: Within the falling, agitated profile, cells without a 3-day rise rose +17.5 % against drift over 20 days (36 cases, t 2.14), while rally cells fell -8.2 %. The difference is -25.7 % (Welch t -4.06). Most of the separation therefore comes from a rebound in the non-rally cells, which is a different situation and off this theme.
findings.F6: The test already used all 19 coins, every fold and the full daily history, so more daily data is not available. The tested idea cannot be rerun on more data.

no_ideas: The give-back after rallies in falling, agitated markets points the predicted way but rests on one window (w18) and is not graded at any horizon (F2–F4). No more daily data exists to sharpen it (F6), and no condition, side or horizon isolates it clearly, so no amended idea on the theme is worth testing.
